seo.title: Claude Code
seo.description: Learn how to use Claude Code to build software with AI. Tips, best practices, and a community-driven roadmap for getting the most out of Anthropic's agentic coding tool.

questions.title: Is Claude Code better than Cursor?

content.text: The choice between Claude Code or Cursor depends on how you work, what you are building, and which interface fits your workflow.

Claude Code is better suited for execution-heavy tasks where delegation and automation matter more. Cursor fits interactive development workflows where fast feedback and visibility into changes are more important. questions.title: When should I use Claude Cowork vs Chat vs Code?

content.text: Claude Cowork, Chat, and Code all run on the same Claude intelligence. But they are designed for different kinds of work. Claude Chat is built for conversation, thinking, and drafting. Cowork handles multi-step knowledge work, documents, research, and file-based tasks, while Claude Code is for developers working with codebases, commands, and software projects. questions.title: Is Claude better than GitHub Copilot for coding?

content.text: Claude and GitHub Copilot are two of the most popular vibe coding tools, but they serve a specific purpose. Claude Code works as a terminal-first autonomous agent built for larger coding tasks. It runs in your terminal and works on its own, reading your codebase and making decisions as it goes. GitHub Copilot, by contrast, works as an IDE-embedded assistant. It supports you as you write, edit, and review code in your editor. questions.title: Should I use Claude Code or Codex?

content.text: are both terminal-first tools for complex coding tasks. The main difference depends on how you like to work. With Claude Code, you get an interactive setup in your terminal or IDE with Anthropic models. But Codex lets you work on your own computer or send tasks to the cloud and run multiple agents in parallel. The better fit depends on lots of factors like your budget, subscription, and usage limits.

questions.title: When should I use OpenCode instead of Claude Code?

content.text: are both terminal-based, agentic coding agents. They read your codebase, edit files, and run commands autonomously from the command line (CLI) rather than a chat window. Where they differ is in how much of the stack you control, which matters if cost, privacy, or vendor lock-in are concerns. Claude Code gives you a managed, streamlined experience built around Anthropic's Claude, while OpenCode gives you more control over your models, providers, and deployment. The right choice depends on what matters most in your workflows, whether that's cost, simplicity, managed access, model flexibility, or greater control.
